sections.heading: How to Play Demonology
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Demonology"][color=c9]Demonology Warlock Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]

Demonology Warlock is a fairly simple generator \u279c spender rotation at its core. With a few short cooldowns, there are just a small handful of rules to follow in general:

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=inv_misc_gem_amethyst_02 size=medium type=round color=c9 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c9]Don't overcap Soul Shards:[/color][/b] [spell=246985] should never sit at their cap of 5 without being spent, or be overcapped by using a Soul Shard [i]generator[/i] while at 4 [spell=264178] or 5 [spell=686]. [i]Spender[/i] Priority is [spell=104316] \u279c [spell=105174].
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=inv_summondemonictyrant size=medium type=round color=c9 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c9]Demonic Tyrant cycle:[/color][/b] Since the buff your [spell=265187] gains is dynamically updated per demon summoned and only extends the duration of [spell=104316], you will want to make sure you have your [spell=104316] out and on cooldown before going into your cooldown cycle. This ensures you extend your [spell=104316] and giving yourself the guaranteed buff to your [spell=265187].
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]

sections.body:
[h2 toc=false type=bar]Pre-Combat Check[/h2]
	Before any combat happens, it is important for Demonology Warlock to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.
	[center][wrapper width=800px][center][box]
	[ul]
		[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Get your food buff and oil applied![/b][/li]
		[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Summon your Felguard![/b][/li]		
		[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Drop healthstones! -[/b] Cast [spell=29893] for every party/raid member to get a [item=5512][/li]
		[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Portals, portals everywhere! -[/b] As needed, make sure your portals are down in an appropriate location. This includes both personal, [spell=268358] and group, [spell=111771] portals.[/li]
		[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Double Check your Talents! -[/b] Have another quick look to make sure you are in the correct talents for the boss, and you can't see any changes that might help.[/li]
	[/ul]
	[/box][/center][/wrapper][/center]
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=c9][icon name=spell_shadow_metamorphosis type=round size=medium inline=true color=c9][/icon] Demonology Warlock Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]

[pad]

[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]

[tab name="Demonic Tyrant" icon=inv_summondemonictyrant]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c9] Demonic Tyrant [/color][/h3]
	[spell=265187] is a staple cooldown and drives lot of our damage sequences. It extends the time of just your [spell=104316] when talented into [spell=1276748]; however, [spell=265187] gains an additional damage modifier for each demon summoned. Maximize this.
[/tab]
[tab name="Grimoires" icon=warlock_grimoireofservice]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c9] Grimoires [/color][/h3]
	[spell=1276452] provides us with an on-demand self-dispel when summoned and deals moderate damage for a two-minute cooldown. While it's on cooldown, you also gain access to [spell=132411], which can help dispel yourself and others in your party in a pinch. [spell=1276467] is likely the more common option of the two simply because it will interrupt the target it's cast on, on demand, and when on cooldown, giving you access to another interrupt in the form of [spell=19647].
[/tab]
[tab name="Implosion" icon=inv_implosion]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c9] Implosion [/color][/h3]
	Our on-demand AoE is only available in the form of [spell=196277]. It is a 15s cooldown and consumes a maximum of 6 Wild Imps to deal AoE damage. Note that this will consume any number of Wild Imps [b]up to[/b] 6, so there is a world where you can implode the non-maximum number of Wild Imps. It is recommended to always implode with the 6 Wild Imp maximum whenever possible.
[/tab]
[tab name="Doomguard" icon=warlock_summon_doomguard]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c9] Doomguard [/color][/h3]
	A powerful AoE cooldown that can be used whenever there are multiple targets. Be aware that it does have a target cap of 5 enemies, so if you cast it with more than 5 enemies around, it will not deal damage to more than those five targets at any given time.
[/tab]
[tab name="Felstorm" icon=ability_warrior_bladestorm]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c9] Felstorm [/color][/h3]
	For more advanced players, turning [b]OFF[/b] auto-cast from [spell=89751] may be beneficial to your DPS in Single Target situations. This is primarily due to the energy it consumes that takes away from additional [spell=30213] casts and a few melee attacks from your Felguard. This tip is [i]EXTREMELY[/i] min-max and is not suitable for every player to use. If auto-cast is turned off and you are in a position to have it hit at least two targets but don't have your Felguard cast [spell=89751], you will negate the other 'gains' you get by having it not auto-cast.
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Tips
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=c9][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c9][/icon] Demonology Warlock Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]

[pad]

[tabs name="advanced" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Demonic Cores" icon=warlock_spelldrain]
	[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c9] Demonic Cores [/color][/h3]
	Since [spell=267102] are our most common proc which enables us to use a more efficient way of building Soul Shards, with this in mind managing this resource is extremely important. Demonic Cores only stack to a maximum of 4 and there are periods where you will want to bank charges of this resource for cooldown windows. For example, you would want a minimum of 2 charges for each time you approach a [spell=265187] cooldown as it will allow you to easily, and quickly, generate additional Soul Shards for more Wild Imps while your Demonic Tyrant is active, increasing its damage.
	Another example of effective use of Demonic Cores is during AoE where you can spread [spell=460551] to multiple targets for additional AoE since each application of Doom is its own damage source.
	Ideally, you will want to hold 2 charges of [spell=267102] as often as possible. This is both a means of having quick resources available to you and allows you to not overcap your charges and waste procs.
[/tab]
[/tabs]
[pad]

Our Demonology Warlock guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on [b]View Changelog[/b] in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Demonology Warlock guides for [b]Midnight Season 2[/b], make sure to browse the [i]Navigation Bar[/i] at the top of the page, along with our list of [b]Related Guides[/b] just beneath the [i]Table of Contents[/i].

[tooltip name=InfernalBolt][color=q]Ensure this won't overcap you on [spell=246985] before casting.[/color][/tooltip]
[tooltip name=DoomSpreading][color=q]Casting your [spell=264178] on multiple targets will spread out your [spell=460551] applications which all do damage independantly.[/color][/tooltip]
